claims.text: Diagnostic: radiolucent air and ⍉lung markings b/n a shrunken lobe or lung and the parietal pleura
claims.quote: Radiolucent air and the absence of lung markings juxtaposed between a shrunken lobe or lung and the parietal pleura are diagnostic of pneumothorax.

claims.text: Sus in a stable pt w dyspnea or pleuritic CP and USU confirmed w an upright inspir chest radiograph; expir films increase lung density and so the contrast w the pleural air
claims.quote: The diagnosis is suspected in patients whose condition is stable but who have dyspnea or pleuritic chest pain and is usually confirmed with upright inspiratory chest radiograph. The density of the lung tissue is increased if expiratory films are obtained, thereby increasing the difference in contrast between the air in the pleural space and the adjacent lung tissue (which has less air due to a combination of the expiratory state and any collapse).

claims.text: Trach deviation and mediastinal shift are seen w lrg pneumothoraces
claims.quote: Tracheal deviation and mediastinal shift are seen with large pneumothoraces.

claims.text: Bedside US can also make the dx if underlying lung dz does ⍉prevent adequate visualization
claims.quote: The diagnosis may also be made using bedside ultrasound if underlying lung disease does not prevent adequate visualization.

claims.text: Lung US: lung sliding / 'seashore' on M-mode = norm pleura (rules OUT pneumothorax @ that spot)
claims.quote: Lung sliding / 'seashore' on M-mode Lung US Normal pleura (rules OUT pneumothorax at that spot)

claims.text: Lung US: loss of lung sliding / 'barcode' on M-mode → pneumothorax
claims.quote: Loss of lung sliding / 'barcode' on M-mode Lung US Pneumothorax

claims.text: Lung US: lung point (transition b/n sliding and ⍉sliding) = pathognomonic for pneumothorax
claims.quote: Lung point Lung US Pathognomonic for pneumothorax (transition between sliding and non-sliding)

claims.text: Eti Air in the pleural space causing partial or complete lung collapse; it can occur spontaneously or result from trauma or medical procedures
claims.quote: Pneumothorax is air in the pleural space causing partial or complete lung collapse. Pneumothorax can occur spontaneously or result from trauma or medical procedures.

claims.text: Primary spont: ⍉underlying lung dz; classically tall, thin men in their teens and 20s
claims.quote: Primary spontaneous pneumothorax occurs in patients without underlying pulmonary disease, classically in tall, thin men in their teens and 20s.

claims.text: 2/2 spont: underlying lung dz; most often rupture of a bleb or bulla in severe COPD
claims.quote: Secondary spontaneous pneumothorax occurs in patients with underlying pulmonary disease; it most often results from rupture of a bleb or bulla in patients with severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

claims.text: Iatrogenic: transthoracic needle aspiration, thoracentesis, central venous cath placement, mech ventilation, CPR
claims.quote: Iatrogenic pneumothorax is caused by medical interventions, including transthoracic needle aspiration, thoracentesis, central venous catheter placement, mechanical ventilation, and cardiopulmonary resuscitation.

claims.text: Sx Dyspnea and pleuritic CP; sm pneumothoraces are occasionally aSx; dyspnea may be sudden or gradual depending on the rate of development and size
claims.quote: Small pneumothoraces are occasionally asymptomatic. Symptoms of pneumothorax include dyspnea and pleuritic chest pain. Dyspnea may be sudden or gradual in onset depending on the rate of development and size of the pneumothorax.

claims.text: Classic exam: ⍉tactile fremitus, hyperresonance to percussion and ↓breath sounds on the affected side; if lrg, the affected side may be enlrg w the trach shifted to the opposite side, and breath sounds may be ⍉
claims.quote: Physical findings classically consist of absent tactile fremitus, hyperresonance to percussion, and decreased breath sounds on the affected side. If the pneumothorax is large, the affected side may be enlarged with the trachea visibly or palpably shifted to the opposite side, and breath sounds may be absent on the affected side.

claims.text: Tx and next step Her chart: needle decompression if tension; chest tube
claims.quote: Needle decompression if tension; chest tube
claims.locator: Chest X-Ray (CXR), Air / Fluid in Pleural Space table

claims.text: Primary spont w.o resp or ♡ Sx: can be safely observed if f/u chest radiographs @ about 4 hrs show ⍉progression, w regular f/u over the following wks
claims.quote: Primary spontaneous pneumothorax that does not cause respiratory or cardiac symptoms can be safely observed without treatment if follow-up chest radiographs performed at about 4 hours show no progression, with follow up regularly over the subsequent weeks.

claims.text: Sxtomatic primary spont: evacuate by cath aspiration, ambulatory devices or tube thoracostomy
claims.quote: Symptomatic primary spontaneous pneumothoraces should be evacuated by catheter aspiration, ambulatory devices, or tube thoracostomy.

claims.text: 2/2 and traumatic: generally tube thoracostomy
claims.quote: Secondary and traumatic pneumothoraces are generally treated with tube thoracostomy.

claims.text: Video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS) and other procedures can help prevent recurr of spont pneumothorax
claims.quote: Video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS) and other procedures can help prevent recurrences of spontaneous pneumothorax
